You will visit El Rosario Church, with its striking modern interior, the National Palace, the National Theatre, and the Metropolitan Cathedral. The route then continues to Joya de Cerén and San Andrés.

The archaeological stops explore Maya history and the way volcanic activity contributed both to the destruction and the preservation of ancient settlements. They reveal different aspects of the societies that left behind temples and other monuments across Mesoamerica.

Duration: 8 hours • Start: 9:00–9:30 a.m. • Language: English and Spanish

A day of sacred waters and jungle trails.

Today is devoted to nature, adventure, and the magic of Yucatán's legendary cenotes. You will travel to Santa Bárbara, a favorite destination near the village of Homún, where a series of remarkable cenotes awaits. Each offers a different window into an underground world the ancient Maya considered sacred. Ride along quiet jungle trails by bicycle or aboard a charming traditional horse-drawn cart (truk), discovering three or four different cenotes along the way. Some are open to the sky, shimmering in the sunlight; others are hidden in caves, echoing like natural cathedrals carved by water and time. Whether you swim beneath the open sky, float quietly, or simply admire the rock formations and crystal-clear water, the experience will stay with you. It is more than a swim: an encounter with nature, history, and yourself.

Tour highlights:

● Explore three or four distinct cenotes surrounded by nature and tranquility.

● Choose your adventure: travel between the cenotes by bicycle or traditional horse-drawn cart (truk).

● Swim in turquoise waters, with each cenote offering its own shape and character.

● Learn about the natural history and cultural significance of these sacred pools.

● Enjoy a day of relaxation, connection, and quiet wonder.

● All logistics are arranged for a seamless, immersive experience.

Included: Shared transportation, admission tickets to the cenotes, and use of equipment (life jacket, bicycle or horse-drawn cart).

Not included: Meals, tips, and personal expenses.

On the way from the airport, the guide will take the group to the Santa Cruz highlands. As we travel through the island's farming areas, surrounded by wild landscapes and diverse flora and fauna, we may spot finches that helped inspire Darwin's theory of evolution, along with other endemic species.

Today we can observe the famous Galápagos giant tortoises in their natural habitat and learn how private farms help conserve these remarkable animals and their environment. Tortoises of different ages and sizes can be seen here: youngsters with gleaming shells and slow-moving older animals with partially cracked shells, traces of long lives.

The well-known lava tunnels are another destination on our journey. These channels formed when lava flowing down the volcano's slopes cooled unevenly, extending from the highlands toward the coast. Erosion has destroyed sections of the lava tubes, but some well-preserved tunnels stretch for up to 1 km. You will see how they formed and explore passages that can be difficult to navigate in places, with fallen rock blocks in some sections. The guide will explain their geological origins in detail.

On the day you arrive in the Galápagos, you will visit the Santa Cruz highlands with a guide on the way from Baltra Airport to the Fiesta hotel. Here you will begin your introduction to giant land tortoises.

Lunch in the highlands is included after the walk. You will then continue to the hotel and get acquainted with the dive center, where you can try on the equipment or check your own.
